question: Should OpenClaw adopt `local`, `container`, `reverse-proxy`, and `node-mode` as release-tested core hosting contracts exposed through `hosting.profile`, environment, and Gateway CLI selection?
rationale: The implementation is coherent and opt-in, but choosing and permanently supporting these named deployment postures, their fail-closed conditions, and the related Plugin SDK contract is a product and support-matrix decision that code review cannot infer.

options.title: Adopt the opt-in matrix
options.body: Approve the four profiles as core support contracts, land the readiness dependency, and review a clean restacked profile-only branch with upgrade proof.

options.title: Keep generic readiness only
options.body: Land only the operator-selected readiness foundation and ask operators to compose criteria directly without named core profiles.

options.title: Narrow the first release
options.body: Approve only local and container initially, leaving reverse-proxy and node-mode for later RFC-backed additions.

recommendation.title: Adopt the opt-in matrix
recommendation.body: Approve the four profiles as core support contracts, land the readiness dependency, and review a clean restacked profile-only branch with upgrade proof.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent history connects steipete to core product direction, configuration contracts, Gateway policy, and public Plugin SDK expansion.
